sanskrit: śibisindhutrigartānāṃ viṣādaś cāpy ajāyata tān dṛṣṭvā puruṣavyāghrān vyāghrān iva balotkaṭān
english: Despondency arose among the Śibis, Sindhus, and Trigartans when they saw those tiger-like men — fierce in strength like tigers indeed.

sanskrit: hemacitrasamutsedhāṃ sarvaśaikyāyasīṃ gadām pragṛhyābhyadravad bhīmaḥ saindhavaṃ kālacoditam
english: Bhīma seized his mace — all of sharpened iron, adorned with golden designs, tall and splendid — and charged at the Sindhava king, driven as if by Death itself.

sanskrit: tadantaram athāvṛtya koṭikāśyo 'bhyahārayat mahatā rathavaṃśena parivārya vṛkodaram
english: Meanwhile, Koṭikāśya wheeled around and attacked, surrounding Vṛkodara with a great array of chariots.

sanskrit: śaktitomaranārācair vīrabāhupracoditaiḥ kīryamāṇo 'pi bahubhir na sma bhīmo 'bhyakampata
english: Though showered by javelins, lances, and iron arrows hurled by the arms of heroes, Bhīma did not tremble.

sanskrit: gajaṃ tu sagajārohaṃ padātīṃś ca caturdaśa jaghāna gadayā bhīmaḥ saindhavadhvajinīmukhe
english: In the vanguard of the Sindhava army, Bhīma slew with his mace an elephant along with its rider, and fourteen foot-soldiers as well.

sanskrit: pārthaḥ pañcaśatāñ śūrān pārvatīyān mahārathān parīpsamānaḥ sauvīraṃ jaghāna dhvajinīmukhe
english: Pārtha, eager to protect the Sauvīra, slew five hundred mountain heroes and great chariot-warriors at the forefront of that army.

sanskrit: rājā svayaṃ suvīrāṇāṃ pravarāṇāṃ prahāriṇām nimeṣamātreṇa śataṃ jaghāna samare tadā
english: The king himself slew a hundred of the foremost, most valiant, hard-striking Suvīras in that battle in the space of a mere blink.

sanskrit: dadṛśe nakulas tatra rathāt praskandya khaḍgadhṛk śirāṃsi pādarakṣāṇāṃ bījavat pravapan muhuḥ
english: Nakula was seen there, leaping down from his chariot with sword in hand, repeatedly scattering the heads of the foot-guards like seeds sown broadcast.

sanskrit: sahadevas tu saṃyāya rathena gajayodhinaḥ pātayām āsa nārācair drumebhya iva barhiṇaḥ
english: Sahadeva, advancing with his chariot against elephant-fighters, brought them down with iron arrows as peacocks are knocked from trees.

sanskrit: tatas trigartaḥ sadhanur avatīrya mahārathāt gadayā caturo vāhān rājñas tasya tadāvadhīt
english: Then a Trigarta warrior, bow in hand, descended from his great chariot and with his mace slew four horses of that king.

sanskrit: tam abhyāśagataṃ rājā padātiṃ kuntinandanaḥ ardhacandreṇa bāṇena vivyādhorasi dharmarāṭ
english: When that warrior came close on foot, the righteous king, son of Kuntī, pierced him in the chest with a crescent-headed arrow.

sanskrit: sa bhinnahṛdayo vīro vaktrāc choṇitam udvaman papātābhimukhaḥ pārthaṃ chinnamūla iva drumaḥ
english: His heart split open, that hero vomited blood from his mouth and fell forward facing Pārtha, like a tree uprooted at its base.

sanskrit: indrasenadvitīyas tu rathāt praskandya dharmarāṭ hatāśvaḥ sahadevasya pratipede mahāratham
english: The righteous king, his horses slain, leapt from his chariot along with Indrasena and took refuge on Sahadeva's great chariot.

sanskrit: nakulaṃ tv abhisaṃdhāya kṣemaṃkaramahāmukhau ubhāv ubhayatas tīkṣṇaiḥ śaravarṣair avarṣatām
english: Kṣemaṃkara and Mahāmukha, targeting Nakula, both rained showers of sharp arrows on him from either side.

sanskrit: tau śarair abhivarṣantau jīmūtāv iva vārṣikau ekaikena vipāṭhena jaghne mādravatīsutaḥ
english: Those two, pouring down arrows like monsoon clouds, were each slain with a single decisive shot by Mādrī's son.

sanskrit: trigartarājaḥ surathas tasyātha rathadhūrgataḥ ratham ākṣepayām āsa gajena gajayānavit
english: Then Suratha, king of the Trigartans, expert in elephant warfare, charged from the chariot's pole and caused his chariot to crash by means of an elephant.

sanskrit: nakulas tv apabhīs tasmād rathāc carmāsipāṇimān udbhrāntaṃ sthānam āsthāya tasthau girir ivācalaḥ
english: Nakula, fearless, leapt from that chariot with shield and sword in hand, took up a commanding position, and stood immovable as a mountain.

sanskrit: surathas taṃ gajavaraṃ vadhāya nakulasya tu preṣayām āsa sakrodham abhyucchritakaraṃ tataḥ
english: Suratha then furiously urged that great elephant — its trunk raised — toward Nakula for the kill.

sanskrit: nakulas tasya nāgasya samīpaparivartinaḥ saviṣāṇaṃ bhujaṃ mūle khaḍgena nirakṛntata
english: As that elephant came close upon him, Nakula severed its trunk at the root with his sword — the trunk complete with its tusk.

sanskrit: sa vinadya mahānādaṃ gajaḥ kaṅkaṇabhūṣaṇaḥ patann avākśirā bhūmau hastyārohān apothayat
english: That elephant, adorned with anklet ornaments, let out a great roar and fell headlong to the ground, crushing its riders beneath it.

sanskrit: sa tat karma mahat kṛtvā śūro mādravatīsutaḥ bhīmasenarathaṃ prāpya śarma lebhe mahārathaḥ
english: Having accomplished that great feat, the heroic son of Mādrī, that great chariot-warrior, found safety by reaching Bhīmasena's chariot.

sanskrit: bhīmas tv āpatato rājñaḥ koṭikāśyasya saṃgare sūtasya nudato vāhān kṣureṇāpāharac chiraḥ
english: In the battle, as king Koṭikāśya bore down, Bhīma severed with a razor-headed arrow the head of that king's charioteer as he urged the horses on.

sanskrit: na bubodha hataṃ sūtaṃ sa rājā bāhuśālinā tasyāśvā vyadravan saṃkhye hatasūtās tatas tataḥ
english: The king did not realize his charioteer had been slain by that mighty-armed one; his horses, driverless, bolted in all directions across the battlefield.

sanskrit: vimukhaṃ hatasūtaṃ taṃ bhīmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ jaghāna talayuktena prāsenābhyetya pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Bhīma, the foremost striker, the Pāṇḍava, advanced and slew that king — turned away and driverless — with a palm-strengthened javelin.

sanskrit: dvādaśānāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ sauvīrāṇāṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ cakarta niṣitair bhallair dhanūṃṣi ca śirāṃsi ca
english: Dhanaṃjaya cut off, with sharp broad-headed arrows, both the bows and the heads of all twelve of the Sauvīra warriors.

sanskrit: śibīn ikṣvākumukhyāṃś ca trigartān saindhavān api jaghānātirathaḥ saṃkhye bāṇagocaram āgatān
english: That superb chariot-warrior slew in battle the Śibis, the foremost of the Ikṣvākus, the Trigartans, and the Sindhavans as they came within range of his arrows.

sanskrit: sāditāḥ pratyadṛśyanta bahavaḥ savyasācinā sapatākāś ca mātaṅgāḥ sadhvajāś ca mahārathāḥ
english: Many were laid low by Savyasācī — elephants with their banners still flying, great chariot-warriors with their standards still raised.

sanskrit: pracchādya pṛthivīṃ tasthuḥ sarvam āyodhanaṃ prati śarīrāṇy aśiraskāni videhāni śirāṃsi ca
english: Headless trunks and detached heads lay strewn across the whole field of battle, covering the earth.

sanskrit: śvagṛdhrakaṅkakākolabhāsagomāyuvāyasāḥ atṛpyaṃs tatra vīrāṇāṃ hatānāṃ māṃsaśoṇitaiḥ
english: Dogs, vultures, herons, crows, kites, jackals, and ravens feasted insatiably there on the flesh and blood of the slain heroes.

sanskrit: hateṣu teṣu vīreṣu sindhurājo jayadrathaḥ vimucya kṛṣṇāṃ saṃtrastaḥ palāyanaparo 'bhavat
english: With those heroes slain, Jayadratha the king of Sindhu, terror-stricken, released Kṛṣṇā and devoted himself entirely to flight.

sanskrit: sa tasmin saṃkule sainye draupadīm avatārya vai prāṇaprepsur upādhāvad vanaṃ yena narādhamaḥ
english: That lowest of men, intent on saving his own life, set Draupadī down amid that chaotic army and fled toward the forest.

sanskrit: draupadīṃ dharmarājas tu dṛṣṭvā dhaumyapuraskṛtām mādrīputreṇa vīreṇa ratham āropayat tadā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira the righteous king, seeing Draupadī with Dhaumya at her side, had the heroic son of Mādrī place her upon a chariot.

sanskrit: tatas tad vidrutaṃ sainyam apayāte jayadrathe ādiśyādiśya nārācair ājaghāna vṛkodaraḥ
english: Then, with Jayadratha gone, Vṛkodara struck that fleeing army again and again, targeting them with iron arrows.

sanskrit: savyasācī tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā palāyantaṃ jayadratham vārayām āsa nighnantaṃ bhīmaṃ saindhavasainikān
english: But Savyasācī, seeing Jayadratha fleeing, restrained Bhīma who was slaughtering the Sindhava soldiers.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca yasyāpacārāt prāpto 'yam asmān kleśo durāsadaḥ tam asmin samaroddeśe na paśyāmi jayadratham
english: Arjuna said: The one through whose offense this intolerable suffering has come upon us — I do not see that Jayadratha anywhere on this battlefield.

sanskrit: tam evānviṣa bhadraṃ te kiṃ te yodhair nipātitaiḥ anāmiṣam idaṃ karma kathaṃ vā manyate bhavān
english: Seek him out — blessings be on you. What purpose is served by felling these soldiers? How do you regard this fruitless work?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity ukto bhīmasenas tu guḍākeśena dhīmatā yudhiṣṭhiram abhiprekṣya vāgmī vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the wise Guḍākeśa, the eloquent Bhīmasena glanced toward Yudhiṣṭhira and spoke these words.

sanskrit: hatapravīrā ripavo bhūyiṣṭhaṃ vidrutā diśaḥ gṛhītvā draupadīṃ rājan nivartatu bhavān itaḥ
english: The enemies' champions are slain; they have largely scattered in all directions. Taking Draupadī with you, O king, let Your Majesty turn back from here.

sanskrit: yamābhyāṃ saha rājendra dhaumyena ca mahātmanā prāpyāśramapadaṃ rājan draupadīṃ parisāntvaya
english: Together with the twin brothers and with the great-souled Dhaumya, return to the hermitage, O king of kings, and console Draupadī.

sanskrit: na hi me mokṣyate jīvan mūḍhaḥ saindhavako nṛpaḥ pātālatalasaṃstho 'pi yadi śakro 'sya sārathiḥ
english: That foolish Sindhava king shall not escape me with his life — even if he shelters in the depths of Pātāla and Indra himself acts as his charioteer.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca na hantavyo mahābāho durātmāpi sa saindhavaḥ duḥśalām abhisaṃsmṛtya gāndhārīṃ ca yaśasvinīm
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: That Sindhava must not be slain, O mighty-armed one, even wicked though he is — remember Duḥśalā and the glorious Gāndhārī.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tac chrutvā draupadī bhīmam uvāca vyākulendriyā kupitā hrīmatī prājñā patī bhīmārjunāv ubhau
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing that, Draupadī — distraught, furious, yet modest and wise — spoke to Bhīma, addressing both her husbands Bhīma and Arjuna.

sanskrit: kartavyaṃ cet priyaṃ mahyaṃ vadhyaḥ sa puruṣādhamaḥ saindhavāpasadaḥ pāpo durmatiḥ kulapāṃsanaḥ
english: If you truly wish to do what is dear to me, then that vile wretch must be killed — that outcast of the Sindhava line, that wicked, evil-minded stain upon his family.

sanskrit: bhāryābhihartā nirvairo yaś ca rājyaharo ripuḥ yācamāno 'pi saṃgrāme na sa jīvitum arhati
english: One who abducts another's wife, who without any quarrel robs an enemy of his kingdom — such a man does not deserve to live even if he begs for mercy in battle.

sanskrit: ity uktau tau naravyāghrau yayatur yatra saindhavaḥ rājā nivavṛte kṛṣṇām ādāya sapurohitaḥ
english: Addressed thus, those two tiger-like men went to where the Sindhava had fled; the king meanwhile turned back, taking Kṛṣṇā with him along with the family priest.

sanskrit: sa praviśyāśramapadaṃ vyapaviddhabṛsīghaṭam mārkaṇḍeyādibhir viprair anukīrṇaṃ dadarśa ha
english: Entering the hermitage, he found it — its rush-mat seats overturned and scattered — thronged with brāhmaṇas headed by Mārkaṇḍeya.

sanskrit: draupadīm anuśocadbhir brāhmaṇais taiḥ samāgataiḥ samiyāya mahāprājñaḥ sabhāryo bhrātṛmadhyagaḥ
english: The greatly wise king, surrounded by his brothers and with his wife beside him, rejoined those assembled brāhmaṇas who were lamenting over Draupadī.

sanskrit: te sma taṃ muditā dṛṣṭvā punar abhyāgataṃ nṛpam jitvā tān sindhusauvīrān draupadīṃ cāhṛtāṃ punaḥ
english: They rejoiced to see the king returned once more, having defeated the Sindhus and Sauvīras and having recovered Draupadī.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛto rājā tatraivopaviveśa ha praviveśāśramaṃ kṛṣṇā yamābhyāṃ saha bhāminī
english: The king, surrounded by them, sat down right there; and the spirited Kṛṣṇā entered the hermitage together with the twin brothers.

sanskrit: bhīmārjunāv api śrutvā krośamātragataṃ ripum svayam aśvāṃs tudantau tau javenaivābhyadhāvatām
english: Bhīma and Arjuna, hearing that the enemy had gone only a kośa away, themselves goaded their horses and charged after him at full speed.

sanskrit: idam atyadbhutaṃ cātra cakāra puruṣo 'rjunaḥ krośamātragatān aśvān saindhavasya jaghāna yat
english: Herein Arjuna performed a feat most wonderful: he slew the horses of the Sindhava who had gone but a single kośa away.

sanskrit: sa hi divyāstrasaṃpannaḥ kṛcchrakāle 'py asaṃbhramaḥ akarod duṣkaraṃ karma śarair astrānumantritaiḥ
english: Endowed with divine weapons, unagitated even in moments of crisis, he accomplished that difficult feat with arrows charged with sacred weapon-spells.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyadhāvatāṃ vīrāv ubhau bhīmadhanaṃjayau hatāśvaṃ saindhavaṃ bhītam ekaṃ vyākulacetasam
english: Then both heroes, Bhīma and Dhanaṃjaya, charged toward the Sindhava — his horses slain, alone, frightened, his mind in turmoil.

sanskrit: saindhavas tu hatān dṛṣṭvā tathāśvān svān suduḥkhitaḥ dṛṣṭvā vikramakarmāṇi kurvāṇaṃ ca dhanaṃjayam palāyanakṛtotsāhaḥ prādravad yena vai vanam
english: The Sindhava, deeply distressed to see his horses slain and beholding the feats of valor that Dhanaṃjaya was performing, mustered his resolve for flight and ran toward the forest.

sanskrit: saindhavaṃ tvabhisaṃprekṣya parākrāntaṃ palāyane anuyāya mahābāhuḥ phalguno vākyam abravīt
english: Watching the Sindhava stride away in flight, the mighty-armed Phalguna gave chase and called out these words.

sanskrit: anena vīryeṇa kathaṃ striyaṃ prārthayase balāt rājaputra nivartasva na te yuktaṃ palāyanam kathaṃ cānucarān hitvā śatrumadhye palāyase
english: With this much valor you dared seize a woman by force? Turn back, O prince — flight does not befit you. How can you flee abandoning your followers in the midst of the enemy?

sanskrit: ity ucyamānaḥ pārthena saindhavo na nyavartata tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti taṃ bhīmaḥ sahasābhyadravad balī mā vadhīr iti pārthas taṃ dayāvān abhyabhāṣata
english: Thus addressed by Pārtha, the Sindhava did not turn back. "Stand! Stand!" — with that cry the mighty Bhīma suddenly charged at him, while the compassionate Pārtha called out to him: "Do not kill him!"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca jayadrathas tu saṃprekṣya bhrātarāv udyatāyudhau prādravat tūrṇam avyagro jīvitepsuḥ suduḥkhitaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Jayadratha, seeing both brothers with weapons raised, ran swiftly — composed on the surface but deeply distressed, eager for his life.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmaseno dhāvantam avatīrya rathād balī abhidrutya nijagrāha keśapakṣe 'tyamarṣaṇaḥ
english: Bhīmasena, mighty and furious beyond measure, leapt from his chariot, gave chase, and seized him by the hair.

sanskrit: samudyamya ca taṃ roṣān niṣpipeṣa mahītale gale gṛhītvā rājānaṃ tāḍayām āsa caiva ha
english: Lifting him up in rage, he dashed the king to the ground, seized him by the throat, and beat him repeatedly.

sanskrit: punaḥ saṃjīvamānasya tasyotpatitum icchataḥ padā mūrdhni mahābāhuḥ prāharad vilapiṣyataḥ
english: As the king revived and tried again to leap up, the mighty-armed Bhīma kicked him in the head as he was wailing.

sanskrit: tasya jānuṃ dadau bhīmo jaghne cainam aratninā sa moham agamad rājā prahāravarapīḍitaḥ
english: Bhīma drove his knee into him and struck him with his elbow; overwhelmed by the force of those blows, the king fell into unconsciousness.

sanskrit: viroṣaṃ bhīmasenaṃ tu vārayām āsa phalgunaḥ duḥśalāyāḥ kṛte rājā yat tad āheti kaurava
english: Then Phalguna restrained the enraged Bhīmasena, saying: "O Kaurava, remember what the king said — spare him for Duḥśalā's sake."

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca nāyaṃ pāpasamācāro matto jīvitum arhati draupadyās tadanarhāyāḥ parikleṣṭā narādhamaḥ
english: Bhīmasena said: This one of wicked conduct does not deserve to live at my hands — this lowest of men who tormented Draupadī, who was entirely undeserving of such treatment.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu śakyaṃ mayā kartuṃ yad rājā satataṃ ghṛṇī tvaṃ ca bāliśayā buddhyā sadaivāsmān prabādhase
english: What can I do, since the king is always merciful, and you too with your childish reasoning forever hinder us?

sanskrit: evam uktvā saṭās tasya pañca cakre vṛkodaraḥ ardhacandreṇa bāṇena kiṃ cid abruvatas tadā
english: Having spoken thus, Vṛkodara shaved five locks of hair from the king's head with a crescent-headed arrow, while he lay speechless.

sanskrit: vikalpayitvā rājānaṃ tataḥ prāha vṛkodaraḥ jīvituṃ cecchase mūḍha hetuṃ me gadataḥ śṛṇu
english: Having thus dishonored the king, Vṛkodara then said to him: "If you wish to live, you fool, listen to the terms I am about to state."

sanskrit: dāso 'smīti tvayā vācyaṃ saṃsatsu ca sabhāsu ca evaṃ te jīvitaṃ dadyām eṣa yuddhajito vidhiḥ
english: "You must declare 'I am a slave' in all assemblies and gatherings. If you do this, I shall grant you your life — this is the rule of the battle-won."

sanskrit: evam astv iti taṃ rājā kṛcchraprāṇo jayadrathaḥ provāca puruṣavyāghraṃ bhīmam āhavaśobhinam
english: "So be it" — with these words the barely-breathing king Jayadratha spoke to Bhīma, that tiger among men, who shone magnificently in battle.

sanskrit: tata enaṃ viceṣṭantaṃ baddhvā pārtho vṛkodaraḥ ratham āropayām āsa visaṃjñaṃ pāṃsuguṇṭhitam
english: Then the Pārtha Vṛkodara bound the writhing, senseless, dust-covered king and placed him upon his chariot.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ ratham āsthāya bhīmaḥ pārthānugas tadā abhyetyāśramamadhyastham abhyagacchad yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Then Bhīma, mounting that chariot and following Pārtha, drove to the center of the hermitage and approached Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: darśayām āsa bhīmas tu tadavasthaṃ jayadratham taṃ rājā prāhasad dṛṣṭvā mucyatām iti cābravīt
english: Bhīma then displayed Jayadratha in that wretched condition; the king laughed on seeing him and said: "Let him be released."

sanskrit: rājānaṃ cābravīd bhīmo draupadyai kathayeti vai dāsabhāvaṃ gato hy eṣa pāṇḍūnāṃ pāpacetanaḥ
english: Bhīma also told the king: "Let it be reported to Draupadī — this evil-minded one has entered the state of a slave to the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: tam uvāca tato jyeṣṭho bhrātā sapraṇayaṃ vacaḥ muñcainam adhamācāraṃ pramāṇaṃ yadi te vayam
english: Then the eldest brother spoke to him with affectionate words: "Release this man of base conduct — if we are of any authority to you."

sanskrit: draupadī cābravīd bhīmam abhiprekṣya yudhiṣṭhiram dāso 'yaṃ mucyatāṃ rājñas tvayā pañcasaṭaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: Draupadī too, glancing at Yudhiṣṭhira, told Bhīma: "Let this slave be freed — you have already given him five tufts of hair by the king's grace."

sanskrit: sa mukto 'bhyetya rājānam abhivādya yudhiṣṭhiram vavande vihvalo rājā tāṃś ca sarvān munīṃs tadā
english: Freed, that trembling king came forward, paid his respects to Yudhiṣṭhira, and then bowed before all the sages assembled there.

sanskrit: tam uvāca ghṛṇī rājā dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tathā jayadrathaṃ dṛṣṭvā gṛhītaṃ savyasācinā
english: The merciful king Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma, then spoke to him — seeing Jayadratha in that state, caught by Savyasācī.

sanskrit: adāso gaccha mukto 'si maivaṃ kārṣīḥ punaḥ kva cit strīkāmuka dhig astu tvāṃ kṣudraḥ kṣudrasahāyavān evaṃvidhaṃ hi kaḥ kuryāt tvad anyaḥ puruṣādhamaḥ
english: "You are no slave — go, you are freed. Never do this again anywhere. Shame on you, you wretch, lusting after women, low-born with base associates. Who else but you, lowest of men, would have done such a deed?"

sanskrit: gatasattvam iva jñātvā kartāram aśubhasya tam saṃprekṣya bharataśreṣṭhaḥ kṛpāṃ cakre narādhipaḥ
english: Knowing that the doer of this evil had lost his spirit — the best of the Bhāratas, that lord among kings, looked upon him and felt compassion.

sanskrit: dharme te vardhatāṃ buddhir mā cādharme manaḥ kṛthāḥ sāśvaḥ sarathapādātaḥ svasti gaccha jayadratha
english: "May your understanding grow in righteousness and may you not set your mind on unrighteousness. Go in peace, Jayadratha, with your horses, chariot, and foot-soldiers."
